1	# Notes file conventions
2	
3	Conventions the agent follows when reading and writing notes files (`TODO.md`,
4	`notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, and the frozen `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and
5	`notes/done.md`, [Frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done)). One source of truth lives here,
6	and [`notes/README.md`](../notes/README.md) points back. Read this before editing a notes file.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
9	at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). Project-local
10	content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
11	
12	## File reads: read the slice you need
13	
14	Long notes files are appended to over time. Read only the slice your task needs. Grep or read
15	further on demand ([why](rationale.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).
16	
17	- **`TODO.md`** (the routine acquaint read): the first ~60 lines covers intro + `## In Progress` +
18	  the top of `## Todo`, its entries in priority order. `Read` with `offset=0, limit=60`.
19	  `## Ideas` sits below `## Todo`. Read further only when chasing a lower entry, an Idea, a
20	  `[N]` ref, or auditing the whole list.
21	- **`notes/todo-backlog.md`**: the long-tail backlog (lower-priority entries below `## Todo`). Read
22	  only when picking up a backlog item, and grep to locate it first.
23	- **`notes/bugs.md`**: the bug list. Small, so read it whole when triaging a bug or chasing the
24	  `## Bugs` pointer in `TODO.md`.
25	- **`notes/done.md`** + **`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`**: frozen history. Scan headings first
26	  (`grep '^## ' notes/chores/chores-NN.md`), then read only the section you need.
27	
28	## Notes references
29	
30	Reference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render: `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]` for
31	several (comma-separated, not `[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's
32	`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)` links stay single-bracketed.
33	
34	## Reference numbering
35	
36	Every note file keeps a file-local `# References` section at the bottom, and its numbers are scoped
37	to that file: the same `[1]` in two files is two independent slots, each pointing wherever its own
38	file defines.
39	
40	- Treat `[N]` as a **footnote**, a slot meaningful only inside its own file's `# References`, so a
41	  citation never reuses another file's number. To cite a target a sibling file references, take your
42	  own next free slot and define it, and the same target may carry a different number in each file.
43	- A `[N]` *inside a code span* (`` `[72]` ``) is a quoted identifier, data rather than a citation,
44	  so it needs no definition.
45	- To point at a section of another file, use an inline link with an anchor rather than a bare
46	  number.
47	- A definition is usually a path with an anchor, and may also be a **same-file fragment**,
48	  `[N]: #<slug>`, which is how a ladder rung links its own subsection ([The In Progress
49	  block](#the-in-progress-block)).
50	- A file's `# References` may be **re-packed** to a contiguous `[1]..[N]` in first-citation order,
51	  walking the file's prose top to bottom. A file-local rewrite: no other file moves, and a new ref
52	  may take the next free number, out of order being fine. Ask before re-packing, and never re-pack
53	  [frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done).
54	
55	## Markdown anchor links
56	
57	GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric characters in place, map remaining spaces
58	to hyphens 1-for-1. Do **not** collapse adjacent whitespace, so `a + b` -> `a--b` (spaces on both
59	sides of `+`), but `a: b` -> `a-b` (only trailing space on `:`). General markdown reference:
60	[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub publishes no official spec for
61	auto-generated anchors. The de-facto reference implementation is
62	[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).
63	
64	## Todo format
65	
66	`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
67	reference links to more detail.
68	
69	- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
70	  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
71	  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
72	  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
73	- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
74	- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
75	  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
76	- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
77	  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
78	- `## Ideas`: unranked.
79	- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
80	- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
81	- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
82	  numbering](#reference-numbering)).
83	
84	Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
85	project's record, and the payload ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
86	`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.
87	
88	An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
89	entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
90	is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
91	verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
92	renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
93	form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
94	bold title, cited by the bold text.
95	
96	Example shape:
97	
98	```
99	## Todo
100	
101	### Add new feature X
102	
103	The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).
104	
105	### Fix bug Y
106	
107	What is wrong and where [[1]].
108	
109	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
110	```
111	
112	## The In Progress block
113	
114	A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
115	([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
116	deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
117	item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
118	required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
119	other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
120	under a program heading, each one deeper):
121	
122	- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
123	- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
124	- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
125	  body carries the final one
126	- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
127	  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
128	  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
129	- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
130	  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
131	  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
132	  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
133	  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest
134	- **deliberation**: how the five above were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
135	  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
136	  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
137	  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
138	  answer
139	
140	A **`Ladder details`** area follows them: one subsection per rung, the closing included, headed by
141	the rung's exact title. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's
142	problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual
143	delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of the landed commit body. The
144	closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and completes at close-out with what
145	closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.
146	
147	A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
148	subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
149	numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
150	SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
151	that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.
152	
153	A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, and the block has no
154	`Ladder details` area: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's
155	anchor ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
156	
157	The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
158	`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
159	
160	## Frozen history: chores and done
161	
162	`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and `notes/done.md` are the records of cycles that ran before the
163	cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
164	They are frozen: nothing is appended, no section is opened, no entry is retired into them, and no
165	ref is backfilled. They stay in place because Todo entries and design notes link into them, and
166	those links stay valid. Read them as history, by the slice you need.

# Notes file conventions

Conventions the agent follows when reading and writing notes files (`TODO.md`,
`notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, and the frozen `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and
`notes/done.md`, [Frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done)). One source of truth lives here,
and [`notes/README.md`](../notes/README.md) points back. Read this before editing a notes file.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). Project-local
content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## File reads: read the slice you need

Long notes files are appended to over time. Read only the slice your task needs. Grep or read
further on demand ([why](rationale.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).

- **`TODO.md`** (the routine acquaint read): the first ~60 lines covers intro + `## In Progress` +
  the top of `## Todo`, its entries in priority order. `Read` with `offset=0, limit=60`.
  `## Ideas` sits below `## Todo`. Read further only when chasing a lower entry, an Idea, a
  `[N]` ref, or auditing the whole list.
- **`notes/todo-backlog.md`**: the long-tail backlog (lower-priority entries below `## Todo`). Read
  only when picking up a backlog item, and grep to locate it first.
- **`notes/bugs.md`**: the bug list. Small, so read it whole when triaging a bug or chasing the
  `## Bugs` pointer in `TODO.md`.
- **`notes/done.md`** + **`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`**: frozen history. Scan headings first
  (`grep '^## ' notes/chores/chores-NN.md`), then read only the section you need.

## Notes references

Reference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render: `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]` for
several (comma-separated, not `[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's
`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)` links stay single-bracketed.

## Reference numbering

Every note file keeps a file-local `# References` section at the bottom, and its numbers are scoped
to that file: the same `[1]` in two files is two independent slots, each pointing wherever its own
file defines.

- Treat `[N]` as a **footnote**, a slot meaningful only inside its own file's `# References`, so a
  citation never reuses another file's number. To cite a target a sibling file references, take your
  own next free slot and define it, and the same target may carry a different number in each file.
- A `[N]` *inside a code span* (`` `[72]` ``) is a quoted identifier, data rather than a citation,
  so it needs no definition.
- To point at a section of another file, use an inline link with an anchor rather than a bare
  number.
- A definition is usually a path with an anchor, and may also be a **same-file fragment**,
  `[N]: #<slug>`, which is how a ladder rung links its own subsection ([The In Progress
  block](#the-in-progress-block)).
- A file's `# References` may be **re-packed** to a contiguous `[1]..[N]` in first-citation order,
  walking the file's prose top to bottom. A file-local rewrite: no other file moves, and a new ref
  may take the next free number, out of order being fine. Ask before re-packing, and never re-pack
  [frozen history](#frozen-history-chores-and-done).

## Markdown anchor links

GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric characters in place, map remaining spaces
to hyphens 1-for-1. Do **not** collapse adjacent whitespace, so `a + b` -> `a--b` (spaces on both
sides of `+`), but `a: b` -> `a-b` (only trailing space on `:`). General markdown reference:
[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub publishes no official spec for
auto-generated anchors. The de-facto reference implementation is
[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).

## Todo format

`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
reference links to more detail.

- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
- `## Ideas`: unranked.
- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
  numbering](#reference-numbering)).

Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
project's record, and the payload ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.

An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
bold title, cited by the bold text.

Example shape:

```
## Todo

### Add new feature X

The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).

### Fix bug Y

What is wrong and where [[1]].

[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
```

## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
under a program heading, each one deeper):

- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
  body carries the final one
- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest
- **deliberation**: how the five above were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
  answer

A **`Ladder details`** area follows them: one subsection per rung, the closing included, headed by
the rung's exact title. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's
problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual
delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of the landed commit body. The
closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and completes at close-out with what
closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.

A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, and the block has no
`Ladder details` area: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's
anchor ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

## Frozen history: chores and done

`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and `notes/done.md` are the records of cycles that ran before the
cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
They are frozen: nothing is appended, no section is opened, no entry is retired into them, and no
ref is backfilled. They stay in place because Todo entries and design notes link into them, and
those links stay valid. Read them as history, by the slice you need.

1	# jj and cross-repo linking
2	
3	How version control is driven on this project (jj, never raw git) and how the two repos' commits
4	point at each other (the `ochid:` trailer). Read this before any jj operation beyond `st` / `log` /
5	`diff`, and always before touching a commit description.
6	
7	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
8	at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). Project-local
9	content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
10	
11	## jj Basics
12	
13	**Use jj, not git, for version-control operations** (status, log, diff, commit, push, history
14	rewrite, [why](rationale.md#jj-basics)). jj coexists with the git backend, so the repo *can* be
15	driven with raw `git`, but this project's workflow (bookmarks, the working-copy `@` model, ochid
16	trailers) is expressed in jj terms.
17	Reaching for `git` invites state that doesn't match the jj documentation here. There is no `jj mv`:
18	to move/rename a tracked file, just `mv` it on disk and jj detects the rename by content.
19	
20	Below, `<repo>` is either side's path and `<agent-dir>` the agent-repo's, which the work-repo's
21	`.vc-config.md` names under `[repos] agent` ([.vc-config.md](#vc-configmd)) rather than any
22	fixed directory.
23	
24	- `jj st -R .` / `jj st -R <agent-dir>`: show working copy status
25	- `jj log -R .` / `jj log -R <agent-dir>`: show commit log
26	- `jj commit -m "title" -m "body" -R <repo>`: finalize working copy into a commit
27	- `jj describe -m "title" -m "body" -R <repo>`: set description without committing
28	- `jj git push --bookmark <name> -R <repo>`: push a bookmark (no `--allow-new` flag: jj pushes new
29	  bookmarks without special flags)
30	- `jj bookmark set <name> -r <rev> -R <repo>`: create the bookmark, or move an existing one, at
31	  `<rev>`. Moving it backwards needs `--allow-backwards`
32	- `jj git push --named <name>=<rev> -R <repo>`: create *and* publish in one step, which is the usual
33	  way a cycle's bookmark is born (see [Cycle bookmarks](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land))
34	- In jj, the working copy (@) is always a mutable commit being edited. `jj commit` finalizes it and
35	  creates a new empty working copy on top.
36	- The agent-repo always has uncommitted changes during an active session because session data
37	  updates continuously.
38	- `jj rebase` uses `--onto`/`-o` to name the destination(s).
39	
40	Viewing, for a review: `jj diff -R .` is the working copy, `jj diff -r @- -R .` the previous commit,
41	`jj show -r <X> -R .` one revision's description and diff. Never `jj edit -r @-` to view a past
42	commit: it marks it mutable and shifts `@`.
43	
44	## Revsets
45	
46	How commits are addressed in `-r` arguments, condensed. jj's own semantics are the one dialect
47	([why](rationale.md#revsets)). The full language is `jj help -k revsets`, the single authority, and
48	the worked tutorial with terminal transcripts is `jj-tips.md`, hosted once in the template
49	repository.
50	
51	- A revision is `@` (the working copy), a chid prefix, or a commit id. Unambiguous prefixes are
52	  accepted, and ambiguous ones are rejected, never guessed.
53	- Neighbors: `@-` parent, `@--` grandparent, `@+` child. A step past the end of the chain is the
54	  empty set, not an error.
55	- `::` is the primary range operator, symmetric and endpoint-inclusive:
56	  - `::x` ancestors of x, including x. `x::` descendants of x, including x
57	  - `x::y` the DAG path: descendants of x that are also ancestors of y
58	- `..` is git-compatible set subtraction, not a tighter `::`:
59	  - `x..y` is `::y ~ ::x`: ancestors of y that are not ancestors of x
60	  - `x..` is `~::x`: every visible commit that is not an ancestor of x. Open-ended, so on a repo
61	    with parked branches it includes commits unrelated to x
62	  - `..x` is `::x ~ root()`: ancestors of x, excluding the root
63	- Useful sets: `jj log` (default revset), `jj log -r ::@` (all ancestors of `@`),
64	  `jj log -r 'all()'` (all visible commits), `jj evolog -r X` (one change's rewrite history),
65	  `jj op log` (operation history).
66	
67	## Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)
68	
69	The cross-reference between the work-repo and the agent-repo is what makes the dual-repo work: every
70	commit points at its counterpart in the other repo, so the "what" (code) and the "why / how"
71	(session) stay linked across time. That pointer is the **ochid** (Other Change ID) git trailer
72	([why](rationale.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).
73	
74	A **chid** is jj's change ID, a permanent identifier that survives rebases and `describe`s (unlike
75	the commit ID / git SHA, which changes on rewrite). An **ochid** trailer carries the counterpart
76	commit's chid behind a prefix naming the repo it lives in:
77	
78	- The prefix names a side, not a location. `/` refers to the work-repo and `/.claude` to the
79	  agent-repo, and each repo's own location is the path the work-repo's `.vc-config.md` declares,
80	  `[repos] work` and `[repos] agent`. The agent one may be any reachable relative path, under
81	  the work-repo's tree or outside it, and the `.claude` in the label is a constant that says
82	  nothing about it, so a sweep over the agent-repo's directory leaves every trailer alone.
83	- Which label a commit takes is decided by reading a repo's own `.vc-config.md`, its
84	  `[repos] agent` resolved relative to that file and compared against the directory holding it.
85	  So the config picks the side and the label is a constant, and the two never need to agree.
86	- `ochid: /<chid>` references a change in the **work-repo**.
87	- `ochid: /.claude/<chid>` references a change in the **agent-repo**.
88	
89	Trailers are blank-line-separated `key: value` lines at the end of the commit body, using the chid's
90	**12-character** prefix:
91	
92	```
93	ochid: /.claude/xvzvruqowktp   # points to an agent-repo change
94	ochid: /wtpmottvxqzl           # points to a work-repo change
95	```
96	
97	How many, and which direction:
98	
99	- **Work-repo commits** each carry one `ochid: /.claude/<agent-chid>`, the agent-repo's change ID.
100	- **The agent-repo commit** carries one `ochid: /<work-chid>` per work-repo commit in that push. The
101	  count is per *push*, not per cycle. A trapezoid close-out whose rungs were pushed 1:1 as they
102	  landed still carries exactly one. More than one occurs when a single push publishes several
103	  work-repo commits.
104	
105	Use `vc-x1 chid -s work,agent -L` to capture the change IDs (first line work-repo, second agent
106	repo).
107	
108	`ochid:` trailers are **stamped by `vc-x1 push`**. Never hand-write them into a commit body or
109	`--title`/`--body`.
110	
111	## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do
112	
113	`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
114	and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
115	of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
116	([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
117	repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:
118	
119	- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
120	  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
121	  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
122	- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
123	  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
124	  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
125	- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
126	  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
127	- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
128	  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
129	    bookmark the work-repo is on.
130	  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
131	    the wrong remote ref.
132	- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
133	  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
134	    the squash.
135	  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
136	  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.
137	
138	A late work-repo tweak after the push (a forgotten edit) needs `jj squash --ignore-immutable` and a
139	re-push, which is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push.
140	
141	## Re-describing: coordinate first, and keep the trailer
142	
143	**Never `jj describe` a commit that is already published or already carries trailers without
144	coordinating with everyone involved first**
145	([why](rationale.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)). It is a history rewrite,
146	and it silently drops the cross-repo link. Describing a fresh local commit that has never been
147	described and carries no trailers is authoring a message rather than rewriting one, and is not
148	covered. That is a [local
149	ladder](../AGENTS.md#local-ladders)'s scratch describe.
150	
151	When a re-describe is agreed, copy any `ochid:` trailers into the new body by hand (the "don't
152	hand-write trailers" rule covers push authoring a message from scratch, not preserving one already
153	stamped). Hit at a coordinated amend (2026-07-29), where the trailer survived only that way.
154	`vc-x1 fix-desc` repairs a dropped one by title match.
155	
156	## Cycle bookmarks: create and land
157	
158	The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section
159	holds the rule and when it applies, and this one holds the commands
160	([why](rationale.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
161	
162	**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named by the cycle title's slug (the anchor
163	algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links), so the block's title heading
164	and the bookmark derive from one bare title):
165	
166	- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the last
167	  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
168	- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
169	  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
170	  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
171	- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is not
172	  ready to be seen.
173	
174	**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent. Every
175	`jj git push` in it is a push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push) and [Hard
176	stop after the final push](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push), its own approval, the
177	closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
178	rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):
179	
180	1. Restore the plain name, when the project renamed ([Dev artifact
181	   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
182	   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
183	   (`@` sits directly above it).
184	2. Reshape per the recorded choice: trapezoid runs the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe),
185	   keep separate needs nothing. A single-step cycle has no choice recorded and its one commit lands
186	   as it is.
187	3. Fast-forward: `jj bookmark set main -r <closeout> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
188	   This push publishes the reshaped commit, so the topic bookmark itself is never re-pushed.
189	4. Install: promote the artifact from `main`, the cycle's last act, run when nothing can enter the
190	   cycle anymore.
191	5. Delete the bookmark, locally and remotely: `jj bookmark delete <bookmark>`, then
192	   `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` ([Bookmark per
193	   cycle](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). The long-lived case below gets the same
194	   disposal once fully merged.
195	
196	- The fast-forward needs no `--allow-backwards`. Needing it means the bookmark is not a descendant
197	  of `main`, and the situation wants a look, not a flag.
198	- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent. No record cites their SHAs
199	  ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)): the landed commits are the record.
200	
201	**Reshape**, while the bookmark is a draft ([Cycles run on a
202	bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)):
203	
204	- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
205	  `jj describe`, so [No re-describe without
206	  coordinating](#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer) stays intact.
207	- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
208	- **Exceptions**, named and moved past: the bookmark has already landed, another branch is stacked
209	  on it, or the ladder is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.
210

the worked tutorial with terminal transcripts is `jj-tips.md`, hosted once in the template
repository.

- A revision is `@` (the working copy), a chid prefix, or a commit id. Unambiguous prefixes are
  accepted, and ambiguous ones are rejected, never guessed.
- Neighbors: `@-` parent, `@--` grandparent, `@+` child. A step past the end of the chain is the
  empty set, not an error.
- `::` is the primary range operator, symmetric and endpoint-inclusive:
  - `::x` ancestors of x, including x. `x::` descendants of x, including x
  - `x::y` the DAG path: descendants of x that are also ancestors of y
- `..` is git-compatible set subtraction, not a tighter `::`:
  - `x..y` is `::y ~ ::x`: ancestors of y that are not ancestors of x
  - `x..` is `~::x`: every visible commit that is not an ancestor of x. Open-ended, so on a repo
    with parked branches it includes commits unrelated to x
  - `..x` is `::x ~ root()`: ancestors of x, excluding the root
- Useful sets: `jj log` (default revset), `jj log -r ::@` (all ancestors of `@`),
  `jj log -r 'all()'` (all visible commits), `jj evolog -r X` (one change's rewrite history),
  `jj op log` (operation history).

## Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)

The cross-reference between the work-repo and the agent-repo is what makes the dual-repo work: every
commit points at its counterpart in the other repo, so the "what" (code) and the "why / how"
(session) stay linked across time. That pointer is the **ochid** (Other Change ID) git trailer
([why](rationale.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).

A **chid** is jj's change ID, a permanent identifier that survives rebases and `describe`s (unlike
the commit ID / git SHA, which changes on rewrite). An **ochid** trailer carries the counterpart
commit's chid behind a prefix naming the repo it lives in:

- The prefix names a side, not a location. `/` refers to the work-repo and `/.claude` to the
  agent-repo, and each repo's own location is the path the work-repo's `.vc-config.md` declares,
  `[repos] work` and `[repos] agent`. The agent one may be any reachable relative path, under
  the work-repo's tree or outside it, and the `.claude` in the label is a constant that says
  nothing about it, so a sweep over the agent-repo's directory leaves every trailer alone.
- Which label a commit takes is decided by reading a repo's own `.vc-config.md`, its
  `[repos] agent` resolved relative to that file and compared against the directory holding it.
  So the config picks the side and the label is a constant, and the two never need to agree.
- `ochid: /<chid>` references a change in the **work-repo**.
- `ochid: /.claude/<chid>` references a change in the **agent-repo**.

Trailers are blank-line-separated `key: value` lines at the end of the commit body, using the chid's
**12-character** prefix:

```
ochid: /.claude/xvzvruqowktp   # points to an agent-repo change
ochid: /wtpmottvxqzl           # points to a work-repo change
```

How many, and which direction:

- **Work-repo commits** each carry one `ochid: /.claude/<agent-chid>`, the agent-repo's change ID.
- **The agent-repo commit** carries one `ochid: /<work-chid>` per work-repo commit in that push. The
  count is per *push*, not per cycle. A trapezoid close-out whose rungs were pushed 1:1 as they
  landed still carries exactly one. More than one occurs when a single push publishes several
  work-repo commits.

Use `vc-x1 chid -s work,agent -L` to capture the change IDs (first line work-repo, second agent
repo).

`ochid:` trailers are **stamped by `vc-x1 push`**. Never hand-write them into a commit body or
`--title`/`--body`.

## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do

`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
    bookmark the work-repo is on.
  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
    the wrong remote ref.
- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
    the squash.
  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.

A late work-repo tweak after the push (a forgotten edit) needs `jj squash --ignore-immutable` and a
re-push, which is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push.

## Re-describing: coordinate first, and keep the trailer

**Never `jj describe` a commit that is already published or already carries trailers without
coordinating with everyone involved first**
([why](rationale.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)). It is a history rewrite,
and it silently drops the cross-repo link. Describing a fresh local commit that has never been
described and carries no trailers is authoring a message rather than rewriting one, and is not
covered. That is a [local
ladder](../AGENTS.md#local-ladders)'s scratch describe.

When a re-describe is agreed, copy any `ochid:` trailers into the new body by hand (the "don't
hand-write trailers" rule covers push authoring a message from scratch, not preserving one already
stamped). Hit at a coordinated amend (2026-07-29), where the trailer survived only that way.
`vc-x1 fix-desc` repairs a dropped one by title match.

## Cycle bookmarks: create and land

The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section
holds the rule and when it applies, and this one holds the commands
([why](rationale.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).

**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named by the cycle title's slug (the anchor
algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links), so the block's title heading
and the bookmark derive from one bare title):

- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the last
  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is not
  ready to be seen.

**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent. Every
`jj git push` in it is a push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push) and [Hard
stop after the final push](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push), its own approval, the
closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):

1. Restore the plain name, when the project renamed ([Dev artifact
   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
   (`@` sits directly above it).
2. Reshape per the recorded choice: trapezoid runs the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe),
   keep separate needs nothing. A single-step cycle has no choice recorded and its one commit lands
   as it is.
3. Fast-forward: `jj bookmark set main -r <closeout> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
   This push publishes the reshaped commit, so the topic bookmark itself is never re-pushed.
4. Install: promote the artifact from `main`, the cycle's last act, run when nothing can enter the
   cycle anymore.
5. Delete the bookmark, locally and remotely: `jj bookmark delete <bookmark>`, then
   `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` ([Bookmark per
   cycle](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). The long-lived case below gets the same
   disposal once fully merged.

- The fast-forward needs no `--allow-backwards`. Needing it means the bookmark is not a descendant
  of `main`, and the situation wants a look, not a flag.
- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent. No record cites their SHAs
  ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)): the landed commits are the record.

**Reshape**, while the bookmark is a draft ([Cycles run on a
bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)):

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so [No re-describe without
  coordinating](#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer) stays intact.
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions**, named and moved past: the bookmark has already landed, another branch is stacked
  on it, or the ladder is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

1	# Versioning
2	
3	How this project versions its commits and the running artifact. The scheme, meaning the cycle suffix
4	spelling and the unique-per-commit aim, is generic and shared across projects: this file is copied
5	**verbatim**, with [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) covering each
6	medium by conditional rather than per-project edits.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and converges
9	at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)). Project-local
10	content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
11	
12	## Terms
13	
14	Three names, used as defined here across [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and the notes files:
15	
16	- **version**: the per-commit version (e.g. `0.3.0-5.3.0`). It lives in the manifest. No ladder,
17	  todo entry, commit title, or commit body writes one (see [Versions live in the version-of-record
18	  only](prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)), and its suffix encodes the cycle
19	  phase for whoever inspects the manifest (see [Suffix scheme](#suffix-scheme)).
20	- **version-of-record**: the authoritative stored copy of the version, in the project's manifest
21	  (see [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)). A built or running
22	  artifact derives from it.
23	- **versioning**: the topic, this scheme as a whole.
24	
25	## A stamp, not a name
26	
27	The version answers "which commit produced this artifact". It is not a name for a step: a step is
28	named by its title and located by its position in the ladder list (see [Steps are named, not
29	numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). So the suffix below is the only number in the
30	system, and since nothing dereferences it, reordering or inserting a step leaves the versions
31	already committed alone.
32	
33	## Advancing X.Y.Z: patch by default
34	
35	Which of the three numbers moves is not a classification problem
36	([why](rationale.md#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default)): **patch by default, minor by the user's call,
37	major by the project's promise.**
38	
39	- **Patch by default**: every cycle advances `Z`, whatever it touched. Code or docs, large or small,
40	  none of it matters, so the choice costs no deliberation.
41	- **Minor is deliberate and rare**: the user names it at a cycle's opening when the change deserves
42	  a visible marker in the history, and the agent never infers it from a change's content or size.
43	- **Major is a project's own call**, since what `X` promises depends on the artifact and its users.
44	  A project that makes that promise records it as its local edit of this rule, and absent one the
45	  default above governs.
46	
47	## Grammar and storage
48	
49	One spelling everywhere the version is written:
50	
51	```
52	<public>[-<suffix>]
53	```
54	
55	- `<public>`: `X.Y.Z`, integers.
56	- `<suffix>`: dot-separated identifiers, each ASCII letters or digits: usually integers (`3`, `3.1`,
57	  `3.1.0`), with an alphanumeric id (`3.hotfix`) allowed sparingly.
58	- **Exactly one `-` in the whole version**, the one that opens the suffix: never a dash inside the
59	  suffix, never a `+` in this spelling. This is the portability invariant that makes the version
60	  storable in every medium below ([why](rationale.md#grammar-and-storage)).
61	- **`v` is a display prefix, not part of the version**: conversation and reports may write
62	  `v0.78.0-3.1` for scannability, while manifests store the bare form. (PEP 440 ignores a leading
63	  `v`. Cargo rejects one.)
64	
65	Storage is a per-medium remap of that one spelling:
66	
67	- **SemVer mediums** (Rust/Cargo): store verbatim. The suffix rides in the prerelease slot, valid at
68	  any dot depth.
69	- **PEP 440 mediums** (Python): remap the single `-` to `+`: `0.78.0-3.1` -> `0.78.0+3.1`.
70	  Mechanical and bijective because there is exactly one dash to find.
71	- **Other mediums**: verbatim if the format allows the one `-`, else the `+` remap. A new medium
72	  adds its case to [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record).
73	
74	Two reservations keep the remap sound:
75	
76	- **The stored version identifies but does not order.** SemVer sorts a suffixed version *before* its
77	  bare release (matching cycle semantics: rungs precede close-out), while PEP 440 sorts the remapped
78	  form *after* it, and reinterprets a lone `-N` as a post-release. Opposite directions, so no
79	  cross-medium logic may compare stored versions. Ordering truth lives in the ladder and git
80	  history. Comparing the public triple alone (e.g. a version gate) is unaffected.
81	- **`+` is reserved** for the PEP 440 remap: no SemVer build-metadata use in Rust repos even though
82	  Cargo allows it, since spending `+` there breaks the bijection with the Python spelling. A repo
83	  that truly needs it declares the deviation in its `custom.md`.
84	
85	## Recording the version-of-record
86	
87	Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
88	case that fits your medium:
89	
90	- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
91	  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
92	  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
93	  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, ...).
94	    Add the case as needed
95	- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored. See [Grammar and storage](#grammar-and-storage):
96	  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
97	  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so `0.3.0-5.3.0`
98	    becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
99	- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
100	  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
101	  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
102	- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see [Unique per
103	  commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement). This project follows the per-commit
104	  preference.
105	
106	## Dev artifact name
107	
108	When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
109	active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
110	clobbers the binary consumers are running:
111	
112	- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
113	  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
114	  `<name>` untouched.
115	- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
116	  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
117	  install dir with stale binaries.
118	- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
119	  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
120	  install.
121	
122	**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
123	`<name>` on `main` only:
124	
125	- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
126	  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
127	- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
128	  installed from what `main` will carry.
129	- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
130	  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.
131	
132	## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)
133	
134	Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
135	running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.
136	
137	- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may bump
138	  less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in [Recording the
139	  version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
140	- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA,
141	  which a commit cannot contain.
142	
143	## Suffix scheme
144	
145	The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
146	encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
147	Preparation**.
148	
149	This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
150	a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
151	number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
152	The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.
153	
154	- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
155	- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
156	- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)
157	
158	**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
159	starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
160	bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
161	needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
162	step without renumbering siblings.
163	
164	Disambiguation:
165	
166	- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
167	- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).
168	
169	**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:
170	
171	- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
172	- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
173	- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
174	- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle
175	
176	Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
177	so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
178	commit carries a distinct version.
179	
180	## Agent-files version
181	
182	The agent-files set has a version of its own, apart from the artifact's, so which set an adopter
183	carries is read from a listing rather than a diff, and an `agent-files` title has a token that is
184	unique by construction ([Project-declared types](prose.md#project-declared-types),
185	[why](rationale.md#agent-files-version)).
186	
187	- **Record**: an empty file, `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z{-suffix}`, the version its name. `ls
188	  agent-data` shows it without a read, a bump is a rename, and
189	  `git log --diff-filter=A -- 'agent-data/agent-files-v*'` lists every version beside the commit
190	  that introduced it.
191	- **Spelling**: `vX.Y.Z` everywhere the agent-files version is written, the file name, an
192	  `agent-files` title, and vc-x1's output, so `agent-files v0.1.0` reads the same in all three. The
193	  `v` is the name-plus-version pair as cargo prints it (`bar v1.0.0`), and a tool's own banner stays
194	  bare (`vc-x1 0.82.0`), so a `v` number is the set's and a bare one the artifact's.
195	- **Proposals bump, adoptions copy**: a proposal cycle bumps it at the opening, advancing per
196	  [Advancing X.Y.Z](#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default), and its rungs walk the [Suffix
197	  scheme](#suffix-scheme) beside the artifact's version, `-0`, `-1`, then bare at the close-out, so
198	  a set copied from a draft bookmark says on its face that it is unfinished. An adoption copies the
199	  source's bare file and bumps nothing.
200	- **Agreed**: the payload's number is the family's agreed version. An adopter ahead of it is
201	  proposing, one behind has not re-synced, and two proposers claiming one number are settled by the
202	  maintainer at convergence, the loser re-proposing under the next.
203	- **Which digit**: tend toward the patch digit, kept to one digit and rolled over into the minor.
204	  We think the minor stays within two digits and major increments when the family decides.
205

  form *after* it, and reinterprets a lone `-N` as a post-release. Opposite directions, so no
  cross-medium logic may compare stored versions. Ordering truth lives in the ladder and git
  history. Comparing the public triple alone (e.g. a version gate) is unaffected.
- **`+` is reserved** for the PEP 440 remap: no SemVer build-metadata use in Rust repos even though
  Cargo allows it, since spending `+` there breaks the bijection with the Python spelling. A repo
  that truly needs it declares the deviation in its `custom.md`.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
case that fits your medium:

- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, ...).
    Add the case as needed
- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored. See [Grammar and storage](#grammar-and-storage):
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so `0.3.0-5.3.0`
    becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see [Unique per
  commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement). This project follows the per-commit
  preference.

## Dev artifact name

When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
clobbers the binary consumers are running:

- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
  `<name>` untouched.
- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
  install dir with stale binaries.
- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
  install.

**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
`<name>` on `main` only:

- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
  installed from what `main` will carry.
- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may bump
  less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in [Recording the
  version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA,
  which a commit cannot contain.

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version.

## Agent-files version

The agent-files set has a version of its own, apart from the artifact's, so which set an adopter
carries is read from a listing rather than a diff, and an `agent-files` title has a token that is
unique by construction ([Project-declared types](prose.md#project-declared-types),
[why](rationale.md#agent-files-version)).

- **Record**: an empty file, `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z{-suffix}`, the version its name. `ls
  agent-data` shows it without a read, a bump is a rename, and
  `git log --diff-filter=A -- 'agent-data/agent-files-v*'` lists every version beside the commit
  that introduced it.
- **Spelling**: `vX.Y.Z` everywhere the agent-files version is written, the file name, an
  `agent-files` title, and vc-x1's output, so `agent-files v0.1.0` reads the same in all three. The
  `v` is the name-plus-version pair as cargo prints it (`bar v1.0.0`), and a tool's own banner stays
  bare (`vc-x1 0.82.0`), so a `v` number is the set's and a bare one the artifact's.
- **Proposals bump, adoptions copy**: a proposal cycle bumps it at the opening, advancing per
  [Advancing X.Y.Z](#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default), and its rungs walk the [Suffix
  scheme](#suffix-scheme) beside the artifact's version, `-0`, `-1`, then bare at the close-out, so
  a set copied from a draft bookmark says on its face that it is unfinished. An adoption copies the
  source's bare file and bumps nothing.
- **Agreed**: the payload's number is the family's agreed version. An adopter ahead of it is
  proposing, one behind has not re-synced, and two proposers claiming one number are settled by the
  maintainer at convergence, the loser re-proposing under the next.
- **Which digit**: tend toward the patch digit, kept to one digit and rolled over into the minor.
  We think the minor stays within two digits and major increments when the family decides.

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there is no `Ladder details` area ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Ladder

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Ladder details

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

# References

[1]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-opening
[2]: #refactor-split-loader-from-parser
[3]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-closing
